passages.text: “Woe to the rebellious children,” declares the LORD, “to those who carry out a plan that is not Mine, who form an alliance, but against My will, heaping up sin upon sin.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD declares a warning.
He warns the rebellious children.
These children make plans.
Their plans do not come from the LORD.
They form alliances.
They do not follow the LORD’s will.
They add sin to sin.
passages.original: ה֣וֹי בָּנִ֤ים סֽוֹרְרִים֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת עֵצָה֙ וְלֹ֣א מִנִּ֔י וְלִנְסֹ֥ךְ מַסֵּכָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א רוּחִ֑י לְמַ֛עַן סְפ֥וֹת חַטָּ֖את עַל־ חַטָּֽאת׃

passages.text: They set out to go down to Egypt without asking My advice, to seek shelter under Pharaoh’s protection and take refuge in Egypt’s shade.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to rebellious children.
These children make plans without asking God.
They decide to go down to Egypt.
They do not ask for God’s advice.
They want to find safety with Pharaoh.
They try to find protection in Egypt’s shadow.
passages.original: הַהֹלְכִים֙ לָרֶ֣דֶת מִצְרַ֔יִם וּפִ֖י לֹ֣א שָׁאָ֑לוּ לָעוֹז֙ בְּמָע֣וֹז פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלַחְס֖וֹת בְּצֵ֥ל מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: But Pharaoh’s protection will become your shame, and the refuge of Egypt’s shade your disgrace.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh is the king of Egypt.
You seek protection from Pharaoh.
This protection will bring you shame.
You look for safety in Egypt’s shadow.
This safety will bring you disgrace.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם מָע֥וֹז פַּרְעֹ֖ה לְבֹ֑שֶׁת וְהֶחָס֥וּת בְּצֵל־ מִצְרַ֖יִם לִכְלִמָּֽה׃

passages.text: For though their princes are at Zoan and their envoys have arrived in Hanes, everyone will be put to shame because of a people useless to them. They cannot be of help; they are good for nothing but shame and reproach.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel sent their leaders to Zoan.
They sent their messengers to Hanes.
They hoped Egypt would help them.
But Egypt is a nation that cannot help them.
Everyone who trusts Egypt will be disappointed.
Egypt will bring them only shame.
Egypt will bring them only disgrace.
Egypt cannot give them any real help.
Egypt cannot save them from trouble.
Trusting Egypt will only lead to embarrassment.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הָי֥וּ בְצֹ֖עַן שָׂרָ֑יו וּמַלְאָכָ֖יו חָנֵ֥ס יַגִּֽיעוּ׃ כֹּ֣ל הִבְאִישׁ עַל־ עַ֖ם לֹא־ יוֹעִ֣ילוּ לָ֑מוֹ לֹ֤א לְעֵ֙זֶר֙ וְלֹ֣א לְהוֹעִ֔יל כִּ֥י לְבֹ֖שֶׁת וְגַם־ לְחֶרְפָּֽה׃ס

passages.text: This is the burden against the beasts of the Negev: Through a land of hardship and distress, of lioness and lion, of viper and flying serpent, they carry their wealth on the backs of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people of no profit to them.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah spoke a message about the animals of the Negev.
The Negev is a dry and dangerous land.
This land is full of trouble and hardship.
Lions and lionesses live there.
Vipers and flying serpents are also there.
People travel through this land.
They load their riches on the backs of donkeys.
They place their treasures on the humps of camels.
They carry these things to Egypt.
Egypt is a nation that cannot help them.
Egypt gives them no benefit.
passages.original: מַשָּׂ֖א בַּהֲמ֣וֹת נֶ֑גֶב בְּאֶרֶץ֩ צָרָ֨ה וְצוּקָ֜ה לָבִ֧יא וָלַ֣יִשׁ מֵהֶ֗ם אֶפְעֶה֙ וְשָׂרָ֣ף מְעוֹפֵ֔ף יִשְׂאוּ֩ עַל־ כֶּ֨תֶף עֲיָרִ֜ים חֵֽילֵהֶ֗ם וְעַל־ דַּבֶּ֤שֶׁת גְּמַלִּים֙ אֽוֹצְרֹתָ֔ם עַל־ עַ֖ם לֹ֥א יוֹעִֽילוּ׃

passages.text: Egypt’s help is futile and empty; therefore I have called her Rahab Who Sits Still.
passages.sermon:
Egypt is a nation.
Egypt offers help.
Egypt’s help is useless.
Egypt’s help is empty.
Egypt cannot save anyone.
I call Egypt “Rahab Who Sits Still.”
Rahab means proud and boastful.
Egypt is proud but does nothing.
Egypt sits still and does not act.
passages.original: וּמִצְרַ֕יִם הֶ֥בֶל וָרִ֖יק יַעְזֹ֑רוּ לָכֵן֙ קָרָ֣אתִי לָזֹ֔את רַ֥הַב הֵ֖ם שָֽׁבֶת׃

passages.text: Go now, write it on a tablet in their presence and inscribe it on a scroll; it will be for the days to come, a witness forever and ever.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Isaiah.
God told Isaiah to act now.
God told Isaiah to write this message on a tablet.
God told Isaiah to write it where the people could see.
God told Isaiah to inscribe the message on a scroll.
This message will remain for the future.
This message will stand as a witness forever.
passages.original: עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא כָתְבָ֥הּ עַל־ ל֛וּחַ אִתָּ֖ם וְעַל־ סֵ֣פֶר חֻקָּ֑הּ וּתְהִי֙ לְי֣וֹם אַחֲר֔וֹן לָעַ֖ד עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: These are rebellious people, deceitful children, children unwilling to obey the LORD’s instruction.
passages.sermon: The people are rebellious.\r\nThey are children who deceive.\r\nThey are children who refuse to obey the LORD’s instruction.
passages.original: כִּ֣י עַ֤ם מְרִי֙ ה֔וּא בָּנִ֖ים כֶּחָשִׁ֑ים בָּנִ֕ים לֹֽא־ אָב֥וּ שְׁמ֖וֹעַ תּוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: They say to the seers, “Stop seeing visions!” and to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us the truth! Speak to us pleasant words; prophesy illusions.
passages.sermon:
The people are rebellious.
They are deceitful children.
They do not want to obey the LORD’s instruction.
They speak to the seers.
They say, “Do not see visions.”
They speak to the prophets.
They say, “Do not tell us the truth.”
They say, “Speak pleasant words to us.”
They say, “Prophesy illusions to us.”
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמְר֤וּ לָֽרֹאִים֙ לֹ֣א תִרְא֔וּ וְלַ֣חֹזִ֔ים לֹ֥א תֶחֱזוּ־ לָ֖נוּ נְכֹח֑וֹת דַּבְּרוּ־ לָ֣נוּ חֲלָק֔וֹת חֲז֖וּ מַהֲתַלּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Get out of the way; turn off the road. Rid us of the Holy One of Israel!”
passages.sermon:
These people are rebellious.
They are deceitful children.
They do not want to obey the LORD.
They speak to those who see visions.
They say, “Get out of the way.”
They say, “Turn off the road.”
They say, “Remove the Holy One of Israel from before us.”
passages.original: ס֚וּרוּ מִנֵּי־ דֶ֔רֶךְ הַטּ֖וּ מִנֵּי־ אֹ֑רַח הַשְׁבִּ֥יתוּ מִפָּנֵ֖ינוּ אֶת־ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel says: “Because you have rejected this message, trusting in oppression and relying on deceit, this iniquity of yours is like a breach about to fail, a bulge in a high wall, whose collapse will come suddenly— in an instant!
passages.sermon:
The Holy One of Israel speaks.
He says this to the people.
You have rejected this message.
You have trusted in oppression.
You have relied on deceit.
Because of this, you have committed iniquity.
Your iniquity is like a crack in a high wall.
The wall bulges and is about to fall.
The collapse will come suddenly.
It will happen in an instant.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יַ֥עַן מָֽאָסְכֶ֖ם בַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַֽתִּבְטְחוּ֙ בְּעֹ֣שֶׁק וְנָל֔וֹז וַתִּֽשָּׁעֲנ֖וּ עָלָֽיו׃ לָכֵ֗ן יִֽהְיֶ֤ה לָכֶם֙ הֶעָוֺ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה כְּפֶ֣רֶץ נֹפֵ֔ל נִבְעֶ֖ה בְּחוֹמָ֣ה נִשְׂגָּבָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־ פִּתְאֹ֥ם לְפֶ֖תַע יָב֥וֹא שִׁבְרָֽהּ׃

passages.text: It will break in pieces like a potter’s jar, shattered so that no fragment can be found. Not a shard will be found in the dust large enough to scoop the coals from a hearth or to skim the water from a cistern.”
passages.sermon:
The Holy One of Israel speaks.
He says your iniquity will be broken.
It will break like a potter’s jar.
The jar will shatter completely.
No one will show mercy to the broken pieces.
No fragment will remain.
No shard will be found in the dust.
No piece will be large enough to scoop coals from a fire.
No piece will be large enough to draw water from a cistern.
passages.original: וּ֠שְׁבָרָהּ כְּשֵׁ֨בֶר נֵ֧בֶל יוֹצְרִ֛ים כָּת֖וּת לֹ֣א יַחְמֹ֑ל וְלֹֽא־ יִמָּצֵ֤א בִמְכִתָּתוֹ֙ חֶ֔רֶשׂ לַחְתּ֥וֹת אֵשׁ֙ מִיָּק֔וּד וְלַחְשֹׂ֥ף מַ֖יִם מִגֶּֽבֶא׃פ

passages.text: For the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, has said: “By repentance and rest you would be saved; your strength would lie in quiet confidence— but you were not willing.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD is the Holy One of Israel.
He speaks these words.
He says, “Return to Me.
Rest in Me.
If you do this, I will save you.
If you are quiet and trust Me, you will be strong.
But you did not want this.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹֽה־ אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בְּשׁוּבָ֤ה וָנַ֙חַת֙ תִּוָּ֣שֵׁע֔וּן בְּהַשְׁקֵט֙ וּבְבִטְחָ֔ה תִּהְיֶ֖ה גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם וְלֹ֖א אֲבִיתֶֽם׃

passages.text: “No,” you say, “we will flee on horses.” Therefore you will flee! “We will ride swift horses,” but your pursuers will be faster.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel speak.
They say, “No, we will escape on horses.”
Because you say this, you will indeed flee.
You say, “We will ride on fast horses.”
Because of this, your enemies will be even faster than you.
Your pursuers will catch you.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֨אמְר֥וּ לֹא־ כִ֛י עַל־ ס֥וּס נָנ֖וּס עַל־ כֵּ֣ן תְּנוּס֑וּן וְעַל־ קַ֣ל נִרְכָּ֔ב עַל־ כֵּ֖ן יִקַּ֥לּוּ רֹדְפֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: A thousand will flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you will all flee, until you are left alone like a pole on a mountaintop, like a banner on a hill.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
He describes what will happen because they do not trust Him.
A single enemy will threaten you.
A thousand of you will run away from that one enemy.
Five enemies will threaten you.
All of you will run away from those five enemies.
You will keep fleeing until almost no one is left.
You will be left alone.
You will be like a pole standing on top of a mountain.
You will be like a banner raised on a hill.
You will be exposed and alone.
passages.original: אֶ֣לֶף אֶחָ֗ד מִפְּנֵי֙ גַּעֲרַ֣ת אֶחָ֔ד מִפְּנֵ֛י גַּעֲרַ֥ת חֲמִשָּׁ֖ה תָּנֻ֑סוּ עַ֣ד אִם־ נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם כַּתֹּ֙רֶן֙ עַל־ רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֔ר וְכַנֵּ֖ס עַל־ הַגִּבְעָֽה׃

passages.text: Therefore the LORD longs to be gracious to you; therefore He rises to show you compassion, for the LORD is a just God. Blessed are all who wait for Him.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is a just God.
The LORD longs to be gracious to you.
The LORD rises to show you compassion.
Blessed are all who wait for Him.
passages.original: וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם וְלָכֵ֥ן יָר֖וּם לְרַֽחֶמְכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־ אֱלֹהֵ֤י מִשְׁפָּט֙ יְהוָ֔ה אַשְׁרֵ֖י כָּל־ ח֥וֹכֵי לֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: O people in Zion who dwell in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. He will surely be gracious when you cry for help; when He hears, He will answer you.
passages.sermon:
The people live in Zion.
They dwell in Jerusalem.
You will not weep anymore.
God is gracious.
He will show you kindness when you cry out.
When God hears your cry, He will answer you.
passages.original: כִּי־ עַ֛ם בְּצִיּ֥וֹן יֵשֵׁ֖ב בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בָּכ֣וֹ לֹֽא־ תִבְכֶּ֗ה חָנ֤וֹן יָחְנְךָ֙ לְק֣וֹל זַעֲקֶ֔ךָ כְּשָׁמְעָת֖וֹ עָנָֽךְ׃

passages.text: The Lord will give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, but your Teacher will no longer hide Himself—with your own eyes you will see Him.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is your God.
The Lord will give you bread in times of trouble.
The Lord will give you water in times of hardship.
Your Teacher is the Lord.
Your Teacher will not hide from you anymore.
You will see your Teacher with your own eyes.
passages.original: וְנָתַ֨ן לָכֶ֧ם אֲדֹנָ֛י לֶ֥חֶם צָ֖ר וּמַ֣יִם לָ֑חַץ וְלֹֽא־ יִכָּנֵ֥ף עוֹד֙ מוֹרֶ֔יךָ וְהָי֥וּ עֵינֶ֖יךָ רֹא֥וֹת אֶת־ מוֹרֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: And whether you turn to the right or to the left, your ears will hear this command behind you: “This is the way. Walk in it.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people in Zion, who live in Jerusalem.
God guides them.
You will hear a voice behind you.
The voice will speak clearly.
It will say, “This is the way.”
The voice will tell you, “Walk in it.”
You may turn to the right.
You may turn to the left.
No matter which way you go, you will hear God’s command.
God will show you the right path.
God will lead you as you go.
passages.original: וְאָזְנֶ֙יךָ֙ תִּשְׁמַ֣עְנָה דָבָ֔ר מֵֽאַחֲרֶ֖יךָ לֵאמֹ֑ר זֶ֤ה הַדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ לְכ֣וּ ב֔וֹ כִּ֥י תַאֲמִ֖ינוּ וְכִ֥י תַשְׂמְאִֽילוּ׃

passages.text: So you will desecrate your silver-plated idols and your gold-plated images. You will throw them away like menstrual cloths, saying to them, “Be gone!”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
He tells them about their idols.
They have idols covered with silver.
They have images coated with gold.
God says they will make these idols unclean.
They will treat the idols as worthless.
They will throw the idols away.
They will throw them away like a cloth used during menstruation.
They will say to the idols, “Go away.”
passages.original: וְטִמֵּאתֶ֗ם אֶת־ צִפּוּי֙ פְּסִילֵ֣י כַסְפֶּ֔ךָ וְאֶת־ אֲפֻדַּ֖ת מַסֵּכַ֣ת זְהָבֶ֑ךָ תִּזְרֵם֙ כְּמ֣וֹ דָוָ֔ה צֵ֖א תֹּ֥אמַר לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then He will send rain for the seed that you have sown in the ground, and the food that comes from your land will be rich and plentiful. On that day your cattle will graze in open pastures.
passages.sermon:
God will send rain.
You have sown seed in the ground.
God will send rain for your seed.
Food will grow from your land.
The food will be rich.
The food will be plentiful.
On that day, your cattle will eat.
Your cattle will graze in open pastures.
passages.original: וְנָתַן֩ מְטַ֨ר זַרְעֲךָ֜ אֲשֶׁר־ תִּזְרַ֣ע אֶת־ הָאֲדָמָ֗ה וְלֶ֙חֶם֙ תְּבוּאַ֣ת הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה דָשֵׁ֖ן וְשָׁמֵ֑ן יִרְעֶ֥ה מִקְנֶ֛יךָ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כַּ֥ר נִרְחָֽב׃

passages.text: The oxen and donkeys that work the ground will eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and pitchfork.
passages.sermon:
Oxen and donkeys work the ground.
These animals will eat salted fodder.
People will winnow this fodder with a shovel.
People will winnow this fodder with a pitchfork.
passages.original: וְהָאֲלָפִ֣ים וְהָעֲיָרִ֗ים עֹֽבְדֵי֙ הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה בְּלִ֥יל חָמִ֖יץ יֹאכֵ֑לוּ אֲשֶׁר־ זֹרֶ֥ה בָרַ֖חַת וּבַמִּזְרֶֽה׃

passages.text: And from every high mountain and every raised hill, streams of water will flow in the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.
passages.sermon:
God will act on a day of great slaughter.
On that day, many people will die.
Towers will fall.
Every high mountain will have streams of water.
Every raised hill will have streams of water.
Water will flow from these places.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה׀ עַל־ כָּל־ הַ֣ר גָּבֹ֗הַ וְעַל֙ כָּל־ גִּבְעָ֣ה נִשָּׂאָ֔ה פְּלָגִ֖ים יִבְלֵי־ מָ֑יִם בְּיוֹם֙ הֶ֣רֶג רָ֔ב בִּנְפֹ֖ל מִגְדָּלִֽים׃

passages.text: The light of the moon will be as bright as the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter—like the light of seven days—on the day that the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds He has inflicted.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
He will heal His people.
He will bind up their brokenness.
He will heal the wounds He has caused.
On that day, the moon will shine as bright as the sun.
The sun will shine seven times brighter than usual.
The sun’s light will be like the light of seven days.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֤ה אֽוֹר־ הַלְּבָנָה֙ כְּא֣וֹר הַֽחַמָּ֔ה וְא֤וֹר הַֽחַמָּה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שִׁבְעָתַ֔יִם כְּא֖וֹר שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים בְּי֗וֹם חֲבֹ֤שׁ יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ שֶׁ֣בֶר עַמּ֔וֹ וּמַ֥חַץ מַכָּת֖וֹ יִרְפָּֽא׃ס

passages.text: Behold, the Name of the LORD comes from afar, with burning anger and dense smoke. His lips are full of fury, and His tongue is like a consuming fire.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is holy and powerful.
The Name of the LORD comes from far away.
He comes with burning anger.
He brings dense smoke.
His lips are full of fury.
His tongue is like a consuming fire.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֤ה שֵׁם־ יְהוָה֙ בָּ֣א מִמֶּרְחָ֔ק בֹּעֵ֣ר אַפּ֔וֹ וְכֹ֖בֶד מַשָּׂאָ֑ה שְׂפָתָיו֙ מָ֣לְאוּ זַ֔עַם וּלְשׁוֹנ֖וֹ כְּאֵ֥שׁ אֹכָֽלֶת׃

passages.text: His breath is like a rushing torrent that rises to the neck. He comes to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction; He bridles the jaws of the peoples to lead them astray.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is powerful and holy.
His breath is strong.
His breath is like a rushing torrent.
The torrent rises up to the neck.
The LORD comes to judge the nations.
He sifts the nations in a sieve of destruction.
He puts a bridle on the jaws of the peoples.
He leads the peoples astray.
passages.original: וְרוּח֞וֹ כְּנַ֤חַל שׁוֹטֵף֙ עַד־ צַוָּ֣אר יֶֽחֱצֶ֔ה לַהֲנָפָ֥ה גוֹיִ֖ם בְּנָ֣פַת שָׁ֑וְא וְרֶ֣סֶן מַתְעֶ֔ה עַ֖ל לְחָיֵ֥י עַמִּֽים׃

passages.text: You will sing as on the night of a holy festival, and your heart will rejoice like one who walks to the music of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
passages.sermon:
You will sing.
You will sing as people sing on the night of a holy festival.
Your heart will rejoice.
Your heart will rejoice like someone walking to the sound of a flute.
You will go up to the mountain of the LORD.
You will go to the Rock of Israel.
passages.original: הַשִּׁיר֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם כְּלֵ֖יל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ־ חָ֑ג וְשִׂמְחַ֣ת לֵבָ֗ב כַּֽהוֹלֵךְ֙ בֶּֽחָלִ֔יל לָב֥וֹא בְהַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ צ֥וּר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And the LORD will cause His majestic voice to be heard and His mighty arm to be revealed, striking in angry wrath with a flame of consuming fire, and with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is powerful and majestic.
The LORD will make His majestic voice heard.
The LORD will show His mighty arm.
The LORD will act with angry wrath.
The LORD will strike with a flame of consuming fire.
The LORD will send a cloudburst.
The LORD will bring a storm.
The LORD will send hailstones.
passages.original: וְהִשְׁמִ֨יעַ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ ה֣וֹד קוֹל֗וֹ וְנַ֤חַת זְרוֹעוֹ֙ יַרְאֶ֔ה בְּזַ֣עַף אַ֔ף וְלַ֖הַב אֵ֣שׁ אוֹכֵלָ֑ה נֶ֥פֶץ וָזֶ֖רֶם וְאֶ֥בֶן בָּרָֽד׃

passages.text: For Assyria will be shattered at the voice of the LORD; He will strike them with His scepter.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is powerful.
The LORD speaks with authority.
Assyria is a strong nation.
Assyria will be shattered by the voice of the LORD.
The LORD will strike Assyria with His scepter.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ מִקּ֥וֹל יְהוָ֖ה יֵחַ֣ת אַשּׁ֑וּר בַּשֵּׁ֖בֶט יַכֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And with every stroke of the rod of punishment that the LORD brings down on them, the tambourines and lyres will sound as He battles with weapons brandished.
passages.sermon:
The LORD punishes His enemies.
He strikes them with a rod.
Each time the LORD strikes, music sounds.
Tambourines play.
Lyres play.
The LORD fights against them.
He uses brandished weapons in battle.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה כֹּ֤ל מַֽעֲבַר֙ מַטֵּ֣ה מֽוּסָדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ עָלָ֔יו בְּתֻפִּ֖ים וּבְכִנֹּר֑וֹת וּבְמִלְחֲמ֥וֹת תְּנוּפָ֖ה נִלְחַם־ בָּהּ׃

passages.text: For Topheth has long been prepared; it has been made ready for the king. Its funeral pyre is deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of burning sulfur, sets it ablaze.
passages.sermon:
Topheth is a place of judgment.
God prepared Topheth a long time ago.
God made Topheth ready for the king.
Topheth has a funeral pyre.
The funeral pyre is deep.
The funeral pyre is wide.
There is much fire in Topheth.
There is much wood in Topheth.
The LORD’s breath is powerful.
The LORD’s breath is like a rushing stream of burning sulfur.
The LORD’s breath sets Topheth on fire.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עָר֤וּךְ מֵֽאֶתְמוּל֙ תָּפְתֶּ֔ה גַּם־ הוּא לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הוּכָ֖ן הֶעְמִ֣יק הִרְחִ֑ב מְדֻרָתָ֗הּ אֵ֤שׁ וְעֵצִים֙ הַרְבֵּ֔ה נִשְׁמַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ כְּנַ֣חַל גָּפְרִ֔ית בֹּעֲרָ֖ה בָּֽהּ׃ס
